classification: Independent static primary-source review; no player execution or hardware experiment

lineRanges.basis: Every write updates write address, bus latch and latch lifetime; MOS8580 fast-mode pipeline branch follows.
Only offsets00..18 dispatch voice/filter controls; higher offsets reach default and pipeline bookkeeping.
Readback offsets19..1C supply POTX/POTY/OSC3/ENV3; other reads expose the latch.
Single-cycle clock handles pending writes and bus latch aging.
Debugger shadow is distinct from readback; register masking and RMW second-store handling.
Write stores array byte; reads dispatch OSC3/ENV3 or return zero.
32-byte register bank shared with synthesis consumers.
Three channel bases stride7; ADSR/control consume offsets4..6.
Pulse helpers consume channel offsets2 and3.
Voice waveform/pitch and routing/volume consume active offsets only.
Alternate digital-wave path also consumes channel frequency-high offset1.
Full-machine host masks to32-byte offset and retains a last-write shadow.

sourceBoundFindings.reSid: Every register write changes latch value/lifetime and write-address state. Offset19..1F has no voice/filter parameter case in the reviewed dispatch, but still participates in pipeline bookkeeping. Readback/default reads and clock aging can observe the latch state.
sourceBoundFindings.sidLite: All32 offsets are retained in a register array. Reviewed synthesis consumers use voice offsets00..14 and shared offsets15..18. Readback is generated OSC3/ENV3 or zero, not the stored array. This backend supplies no matching reSID bus-latch/decay implementation.
sourceBoundFindings.hostShadows: VICE siddata and libsidplayfp lastpoke are write-history/debugger shadows. They must not be interpreted as the actual POT/OSC/ENV device readback state.
sourceBoundFindings.rmw: VICE explicitly handles the extra RMW bus write before the final store. The RAM-only auditor must keep SID/I/O reads and RMW rejected rather than treating RMW as a single normal store.

canonicalWindowContract.allowedOperation: Ordinary non-RMW CPU stores to exactly one declared chip canonical window, retaining each original absolute address/value in ordered evidence.
canonicalWindowContract.addressPredicate: any(base <= address < base + 32 for base in declaredSidBases); do not mask an undeclared address into acceptance

offsetClasses.19..1C: POTX, POTY, OSC3, ENV3 readback addresses; writes still have bus state consequences
offsetClasses.1D..1F: Unused register offsets; writes still have bus state consequences

unchangedRejections: Any I/O write outside explicitly declared chip windows
Undeclared mirrors, including D420..D43F when only D400 is declared
Existing payload, entry, clock, model, banking and selected-subtune requirements
canonicalWindowContract.compatibilityBoundary: The selected policy deliberately expands canonical32-byte store admission for strict and pal-banked profiles. Format, selection, banking, reads and RMW restrictions remain unchanged. Standard Flashdance now records its two D419/D41A initialization bus writes; its pinned diagnostic retains the explicit bounded exclusion receipt. This is changed admission, not unchanged legacy rejection.
canonicalWindowContract.evidenceBoundary: Preserve all writes, including readback/unused offsets, rather than silently excluding them. A software write shadow is not simulated SID state.

recommendedGuards: Non-RMW stores at offsets18,19,1C,1D,1F are recorded in order; offset20 rejects for a single declared chip
A second declared chip has its own exact32-byte window; absence of that declaration rejects its addresses
Reads at every canonical offset and undeclared I/O still reject
SID RMW remains rejected and no partial accepted-ledger claim is made
Verify strict Flashdance records both D419/D41A bus writes while its pinned diagnostic still enforces the exact two zero-write exclusion and source pin.
Independent VICE writer trace retains the same init/play offset19..1F stores
limits: This supports an explicit write-admission/ledger boundary, not a simulated bus latch or readback implementation.
Emulator-specific lifetime/pipeline details are not universal measured-silicon guarantees.
No claim that readback/unused writes have no effect, or that extending CPU admission proves PCM/hardware identity.
No Ghouls instruction, initializer-clear-loop or musical-mechanism claim follows from this static emulator review.
publicBoundary: Only source URLs, fingerprints, exact line ranges and interpretation retained; no full third-party source file or reference payload copied.
